prompt: Produce a new list of running totals: element i of the result is the sum of the first i+1 input numbers.
explanation: A running total needs only one accumulator variable that lives outside the loop: add each element to it, then record its current value in the result list. This computes every prefix sum in a single pass instead of re-summing from the start for each position. The input is only read, never written, so the original list is preserved.
hints: Keep an int total = 0 accumulator declared before the loop.
For each element: first add it to total, then add total to the result list.
The result is a new ArrayList; never call set or add on the input list.
